sources.author: rufus
sources.title: Wisdom and AI
sources.description: A Second Renaissance research agenda led by Rufus Pollock of Life Itself. One governing question, four core questions and their subquestions explore alignment, risk and pace, broader impacts and consciousness. Wisdom traditions means especially Buddhism in this source, while inviting others. It asks questions rather than establishing answers. Captured 25 October 2026.

sources.author: david
sources.title: Analysis of the Wisdom and AI map
sources.description: David Joseph’s supplied review of the first map, 25 October 2026. Sections 1–6 propose a substantive goal, competing diagnoses, a candidate release conflict, conditional interventions and a negative branch, prerequisites and conditional transition steps. These are proposed contributions; the review supplies no empirical supporting observations, recognised decision, selected practice or test commitment.

goal.title: Wise decisions need substantive judgment
goal.summary: Four research strands and three supporting conditions are candidates to justify, not established necessities or sufficient conditions.

current_reality.title: Uncertainty is one possible explanation
current_reality.summary: The existing uncertainty branch remains a hypothesis. Uncertainty could also encourage restraint.

current_reality.title: Contested ends and implicit values
current_reality.summary: Test whether apparently technical disagreements conceal ethical disagreements; the joint cause is not established.

current_reality.title: Recognised risk under competitive pressure
current_reality.summary: Pressure, perceived disadvantage and weak coordination form a candidate joint explanation. No supporting observations are supplied.

current_reality.title: Delegation and opportunities to practise judgment
current_reality.summary: Some uses might weaken agency; AI assistance could also strengthen judgment. Distinguish uses, mechanisms and conditions.

current_reality.title: Moral uncertainty and missing criteria
current_reality.summary: Test whether uncertainty and absent criteria lead to inconsistent treatment, rather than treating this as a finding.

conflict.title: A candidate release decision
conflict.summary: The actor, capability and release decision are still unspecified. Both needs require recognition by relevant participants; review points do not resolve this cloud by themselves.

future_reality.title: Review can matter only with supporting conditions
future_reality.summary: Review points AND usable evidence AND authority and incentives AND feasible alternatives are proposed joint conditions. This is not a guarantee or an observed effect.

future_reality.title: Make aims and disagreements inspectable
future_reality.summary: Test the mechanism from explicit aims, through exposed assumptions, to assessment against defensible criteria.

future_reality.title: Specify what a wisdom-derived practice would change
future_reality.summary: No particular practice or tradition has been selected. Its mechanism, limits and relevant aspect of judgment must be specified and tested.

future_reality.title: Change options and incentives
future_reality.summary: Proportionate safeguards or coordination might make restraint or redirection practicable. These are hypotheses, not confirmed effects.

future_reality.title: Review could create false reassurance
future_reality.summary: Formal review may create unwarranted reassurance and premature action. The two unconnected design requirements address those risks; intended coverage is not proof they work.

prerequisite.title: What must be in place for a responsible test
prerequisite.summary: These are candidate obstacles and requirements for an unselected setting. Clear outcomes and a plausible practice mechanism are needed before selecting a feasible intervention.

transition.title: Choose one decision
transition.summary: Conditional plan only. Owners and dates remain unassigned; incoming order links do not establish causation. If a safe test is unavailable, gather information or improve safeguards.

overview.title: Find what sustains the problem in one setting.
overview.text: The uncertainty branch remains alongside hypotheses about contested ends, competition, delegation and moral uncertainty. The source questions establish none of these findings.

overview.title: Examine the needs behind release and restraint.
overview.text: For a capability and release decision still to be specified, test whether timely benefits and protection really require incompatible positions. Relevant participants have not recognised this cloud.

overview.title: Make interventions answer the diagnosis.
overview.text: Review needs supporting conditions. Explicit aims, a specified wisdom-derived practice, and safeguards or coordination offer other hypotheses. Formal review could also create false reassurance and premature action.
link: Inspect mechanisms, joint conditions and the negative branch →

overview.eyebrow: From reasoning to a bounded inquiry
overview.title: Establish what is needed before assigning action.
overview.text: The prerequisite and transition drafts identify candidate requirements and conditional steps. No actor, capability, test setting or wisdom practice has been selected; no owner, date or action commitment is recorded. A stronger diagnosis may lead us to reject review points.

overview.title: Keep the research agenda and the supplied analysis distinct.
overview.text: Rufus Pollock’s research project supplies the original questions. David Joseph supplied the six-tree analysis and its proposed additions; the AI structured the map and originated the retained initial proposals. Neither source credit nor approval to implement endorses the reasoning. Supporting empirical evidence has not been supplied.
